pageCache.pageTitle: School Values | Oake, Bradford & Nynehead CE (VC) Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Values
"Let your light shine"
School Values
Love Friendship Thankfulness Fellowship Resilience Courage Trust Respect
We believe all children can shine at Oake, Bradford and Nynehead Primary School and we strive for every member of our school family to succeed and flourish with us. At the heart of our school vision are our eight core values.
These core Christian values were chosen by our school family and we aim to embody them in all we do. They guide us, ground us and bind us. Therefore every family from across our community, including those of different faiths and no faith, are welcomed at Oake Bradford and Nynehead. That sense of family and our core values help us to foster the warm, nurturing atmosphere which allows our children to thrive and succeed
School Values Prayers
Thank you that we are not alone. Help us to work together,
to listen to one another, and to care for everyone in our school family.
Thank you for your love for each of us.
Help us to show love through kind words, gentle actions, and caring hearts, just as you love us. Amen.
Help us to trust you when things feel hard or uncertain.
Help us to trust one another, to be honest, kind, and dependable friends.
Thank you for our friends.
Help us to be good friends too, to share, forgive, include, and care,
following Jesus’ example.
When things feel difficult, give us strength to keep going.
Help us to learn from mistakes and believe we can try again.
Give us courage to do what is right, even when it is hard or scary.
Help us to stand up for others and to make wise choices each day.
Thank you for all the good things in our lives our families, our friends, and our school.
Help us to notice the good around us and to say thank you every day. Amen.
Help us to respect ourselves,
others, and the world you created.
Teach us to treat everyone with kindness,
care, and understanding.
Thank you for looking after our school. Help us to learn, play and share together so that the world you have made becomes more beautiful every day.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome | Oake, Bradford & Nynehead CE (VC) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
On behalf of our children, staff and governors, I am delighted to welcome you to Oake, Bradford & Nynehead CE (VC) Primary School.
We are a small, friendly three-class village school with a real family feel. Being a small school means that we know our children well, celebrate what makes each of them unique and support them to grow in confidence, achieve their best and feel proud to belong.
Our Christian vision, inspired by Matthew 5:16, “Let your light shine”, is at the heart of school life. Our Christian values help guide the way we learn, work and care for one another, alongside the British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance.
We are proud of our broad and engaging curriculum and, although we are a small school, we make sure our children have plenty of opportunities beyond the classroom. These include Forest School, theatre trips, sporting opportunities, visitors and special events, as well as a residential experience for children in Years 4–6.
We have good links with our local churches and communities, and we value the important part that families play in school life.
Above all, we want our school to be a place where children are happy, safe, curious and confident, where they are encouraged to aim high, care for others and truly let their light shine.
Thank you for visiting our website. We hope you enjoy finding out more about our school and we warmly welcome families to come and visit us.
Headteacher Oake, Bradford & Nynehead CE (VC) Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: What does it mean to be a Church school? | Oake, Bradford & Nynehead CE (VC) Primary School
pageCache.text:
What does it mean to be a Church school?
"Let your light shine"
Love Friendship Thankfulness Fellowship Resilience Courage Trust Respect
What makes us a distinctive Church of England primary school?
Our Christian vision
“Let your light shine” — Matthew 5:16
At Oake, Bradford and Nynehead, we want every child to feel valued and know that they have something to offer. Our Christian vision encourages us to recognise each child’s strengths, support them through challenges and help them grow in confidence.
We put this into practice through our teaching, relationships and involvement in the community. Shining our light might mean persevering with something new, welcoming someone into a game or speaking up when something is unfair.
We welcome children and families of all faiths and none. Children are encouraged to ask questions, explore beliefs and listen thoughtfully to different views.
Our vision in action
Each week, adults across the school nominate children for a Christian Values Certificate to recognise thoughtful choices and actions.
A Year 6 child recently received a certificate for fellowship after consistently helping Reception children settle into their new lunchtime routines. Another child received a certificate for love after supporting a classmate during guided reading.
Sharing these examples helps children reflect on what our values mean. They see that our values are more than words: they shape how we treat one another each day.
Collective worship and assemblies
Coming together gives us time to reflect, sing, share stories and celebrate our school community. Our Christian vision is at the heart of collective worship.
Our weekly programme is:
Story assembly led by Mrs Bond
Singing worship led by Miss Wheeler
No Outsiders assembly led by Mrs Lemon
Sharing and celebration assembly led by Mrs Bond
Celebrating our children
Our Friday assembly is a chance to celebrate children’s learning, effort and contributions to school life. Alongside our Christian Values Certificates, we award British Values Certificates.
These recognise children’s developing understanding of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. Everyday examples might include taking part fairly in a class vote, respecting another person’s views or explaining why rules help keep everyone safe.
We want every child to know that their efforts and the kindness they show are noticed and valued.
School Vision Prayer
Thank you for your love and care for us.
Help us to be lights in the world today,
to be kind when others feel sad,
to be gentle when things are hard,
and to share love wherever we go.
Guide our words, our choices, and our hearts,
so your light can shine through us.

pageCache.pageTitle: English Reading | Oake, Bradford & Nynehead CE (VC) Primary School
pageCache.text:
English Reading
English Reading
Progression in reading
Intent, Implementation and impact of phonics and reading.
We believe that ability to read is fundamental to our children succeeding; enabling them to access the next stage of their education and beyond. Our curriculum has been designed to ensure that pupils have opportunities to develop a love of reading. Our aim is to ensure that pupils gain a thirst for reading a range of genres and participating in discussions about the books; exploring the language used by different authors and the impact the written words have on the reader. Our curriculum has also been designed to ensure that pupils not only read for pleasure but to use books to research and gather new knowledge to extend their understanding.
Phonics (reading and spelling)
At Oake, Bradford and Nynehead Primary School we believe that all our children can become fluent readers and writers. This is why we teach EYFS and Year 1 reading through Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which is a systematic and synthetic phonics programme. We start teaching phonics in Nursery/Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.
As a result, all our children are able to tackle any unfamiliar words as they read. We also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside of the phonics lesson and across the curriculum. We have a strong focus on language development for our children because we know that speaking and listening are crucial skills for reading and writing in all subjects.
Foundations for phonics in Little Acorns Preschool
Daily phonics lessons in Reception and Year 1
Guided Reading in Years 2-6:
Children develop a pleasure of reading
‘Reading for pleasure is the single most important indicator of a child’s success.’ (OECD 2002)
‘The will influences the skill and vice versa.’ (OECD 2010)
We value reading for pleasure highly and work hard as a school to grow our Reading for Pleasure pedagogy.
We read to children every day. We choose these books carefully as we want children to experience a wide range of books, including books that reflect the children at our school and our local community as well as books that open windows into other worlds and cultures. Our English curriculum encourages a love for reading following the Literacy Tree scheme of learning where each unit is created around a short story or book.
At Oake, Bradford and Nynehead Primary School we value reading as a crucial life skill. We encourage our children to see themselves as readers for both pleasure and purpose. Good comprehension draws from linguistic knowledge (in particular of vocabulary and grammar) and on knowledge of the world.
We teach reading to children as a whole class, starting from when they have completed the Little Wandle Fluency Test. We follow the Grammarsuarus reading scheme.
Through the teaching of systematic phonics, our aim is for children to become fluent readers by the end of Key Stage One. This way, children can focus on developing their fluency and comprehension as they move through the school. Attainment in reading is measured using the statutory assessments at the end of Key Stage One and Two. These results are measured against the reading attainment of children nationally. Phonics Phonics Screening Test at the end of Year 1. Half termly checks to ensure that pupils are places within the correct teaching group and that progress is being made
Assessment is used to monitor progress and to identify any child needing additional support as soon as they need it.

RSHE Information for Parents
Children
Kestrel (Year 5 and Year 6)
RSHE Information for Parents
RSHE planning
This half term, we will be covering areas of the Department for Education's RSHE (Relationships, Sex and Health Education) curriculum in both science and PSHE.
In science, we are learning about how the body develops from being a baby to old age. This includes the physical changes of puberty, but also other changes that occur to the body as it grows up. It also includes sexual reproduction. Due to the fact that all of the changes associated with puberty can be overwhelming, each area of physical changes will be taught through mini-lessons. Note: Not all science lessons for the next half term are on the plan (only those relating to puberty and sexual reproduction).
In PSHE, we are learning about 'growing up and changing'. This includes the children's emotional needs when going through changes (whether puberty or other forms of change), mental wellbeing and staying safe. Some lessons will also consolidate their understanding of puberty.
To support the children with the changes of puberty, there are books that the children can borrow for an evening/weekend. A list of books available can be found at the bottom of the page.
A plan of the lessons taught can be found below for each year group.
If you have any questions or clarifications, please let the school know by emailing the school office or through messaging me on Class Dojo.

Puberty can be daunting for the children to discuss. Therefore, below you will find a list of books that the children can borrow upon request.
